absent: Full disposition paths in shrink_folio_list beyond the visible prefix including keep, activate, reclaim, demote, writeback and retry outcomes.
Complete field layouts and numeric values for scan control, lruvec, folio, zone, node, memcg, migrate types, LRU ids and VM event counters.
Lock types, acquisition ordering with other subsystems, interrupt and context constraints, and sleep rules beyond observed pairings.
Behavior of referenced checks, evictable tests, dirty and writeback classification, demotion migration, uncharge, single page free and throttle wakeup paths not shown.
Trace payload schemas and accounting rollup rules across node, zone, memcg and lruvec levels.

findings.text: Global helper that records a signed delta for a node statistic at node level and, when memcg accounting is enabled, also at memcg lruvec level. Callers use it for scan, steal, demote, rotate, refill and deactivate accounting.

Global per cpu event counter for a memcg. It maps the event id to a per cpu slot, returns early when memcg is disabled or the slot is invalid with a one time warning, otherwise adds the count on the local cpu, marks rstat updated, emits a trace and restores cpu state.
Global helper that returns an isolated folio to the LRU and drops the extra reference acquired during isolation.

Global batch free path. It prepares each folio, sends unsuitable orders directly to single page free, groups the remainder by zone under per cpu cache locks with direct free fallback, normalizes high migrate types to movable, commits through the frozen page path, then reinitializes the batch.
Global helper that ages shadow state by adding a page count to the nonresident age of the given lruvec and then walks parent lruvecs to age each ancestor as well.

Global throttling wait keyed by node and reason. It bypasses waiting with a reschedule for user workers and non kswapd kthreads, selects a timeout per reason with special handling for writeback and no progress, then sleeps uninterruptibly on the matching queue and emits a trace.
Global estimate of reclaimable pages in a zone by summing active and inactive file counts and, only when anon reclaim is possible for the zone node, adding active and inactive anon counts.

Global query for swap headroom visible to a memcg. It starts from the global swap page count, returns it directly when memcg is disabled or combined accounting is in use, otherwise clamps it by each ancestor up to but excluding root using configured maximum minus current use.
Global filter that intersects a caller supplied node mask with nodes allowed by the memcg cgroup, doing nothing when the memcg pointer is null and tolerating races with cgroup or hotplug changes.
Global query reporting demotion target nodes for a node as the lower tier mask of its memory tier under RCU protection, reporting an empty mask when no tier is present.

Internal dispatch between active and inactive reclaim for one LRU. For active lists it honors a per type may deactivate mask, invoking active shrink when allowed and otherwise recording that deactivation was skipped and returning no reclaim; for inactive lists it delegates to inactive shrink and returns its reclaimed count.

Internal entry for reclaiming one inactive LRU with a scan budget. Entered with lruvec and scan control, it returns reclaimed pages after throttle wait, drain, isolate, folio list reclaim, putback, accounting, writeback handling and tracing.

Internal entry for scanning one active LRU with a scan budget. Entered with lruvec, scan control and LRU id, it returns nothing after drain, isolate, per folio triage, requeue to staging, accounting and tracing.

LRU vector IRQ protection surrounds isolation and size updates. Active and inactive shrink drain first, take the lruvec IRQ lock, call isolation which walks and moves entries and updates sizes, record isolate and scan counts, then release before per folio processing.

Requeue path holds at most one lruvec IRQ lock at a time and switches it as folios from different vectors appear. It establishes LRU membership before testing for last reference to preserve list integrity against concurrent release, unlocks around putback and batch free plus uncharge, and releases any held lock before returning.

Batch free serializes per cpu caches with per zone trylock semantics. It drops the current cache lock when the zone changes or an isolate type appears, frees isolate types and lock failures directly, and always releases a held cache lock before returning. Tier target lookup uses RCU read lock around dereference.

Isolation walks from the head of the selected LRU up to a page budget, counting every folio size toward total scanned but only eligible sizes toward progress. It diverts a bounded number of folios above the reclaim zone index to skipped staging later spliced back to the head, skips entries without LRU membership or mapped entries when unmap is forbidden, handles pin and clear races, and records per zone taken counts and skip events.
Size maintenance subtracts per zone taken counts from the tracked size of the source LRU, skipping zones with zero taken.
Two compile alternatives exist for a predecessor prefetch hint during isolation: one prefetches the previous entry field when the predecessor is not the list head, the other expands to nothing.
Executable file test is true only when collected mapping flags indicate execution and the folio resides on a file LRU.

Reclaimer identity maps to a constant offset added to base scan, steal and demote counters: kswapd uses zero, khugepaged and proactive use their respective steal counter distances, direct reclaim is the default. A compile check asserts that steal, demote and scan distances agree for direct, khugepaged and proactive.

Anon reclaim is allowed when swap headroom exists globally for null memcg or per memcg otherwise; when no swap headroom exists it falls back to whether demotion is possible. Demotion requires a valid node, a global enable flag, scan permission, a non empty tier target mask, and after memcg filtering a remaining allowed node.

Throttling for lack of progress is skipped when kswapd is hopeless or when pending writeback is small relative to reclaimable pages across managed zones; otherwise the caller waits. The reclaimable estimate sums file LRUs and conditionally anon LRUs.

Active shrink stages isolated folios into hold, active and inactive lists. For each folio it yields, detaches it, returns non evictable folios immediately, optionally releases buffers under global pressure when the folio needs release, rotates referenced executable file folios back to active while counting rotated pages, and otherwise clears active, marks workingset and stages for deactivation. Afterwards it requeues both staging lists, accounts deactivate and rotate events, releases isolate counts and traces the outcome.

Inactive shrink first waits while too many folios are already isolated, aborting with zero after one stall or with a cluster constant if a fatal signal is pending. It then drains, isolates under lock, records isolate and scan counters distinguished by reclaimer, returns zero when nothing was taken, otherwise reclaims through the folio list path, requeues survivors, records demote, steal and rotate deltas, handles writeback from the taken count, and traces the result.

Requeue iterates a staging list to empty. For each entry it ensures the correct lruvec lock, asserts LRU membership is currently clear, detaches it, returns non evictable entries via putback, otherwise marks LRU membership, frees last reference entries via deferred split removal batched with uncharge and free, and otherwise adds survivors back to the LRU while aging nonresident state for still active entries and counting moved pages.

Batch free has a prepare pass then a commit pass. Prepare drops entries that fail preparation and directly frees orders not allowed on per cpu caches, stashing allowed orders in private storage and compacting the batch. Commit walks the compacted batch, resolves zone and migrate type per folio, switches cache locks on zone change, normalizes high migrate types, and commits each page with fallback to direct free when the commit path releases the lock.

Throttle reason selects timing and bookkeeping: writeback uses a tenth second delay with first waiter baseline capture and decrement on exit; congested and no progress share a one tick delay after a bypass check; isolated uses a fiftieth second delay; unknown reasons warn and use a one second delay. All reasons sleep on the matching per node queue and trace requested versus elapsed delay.

Visible prefix of folio list reclaim initializes free, return and demote staging, zeroes statistics, yields, and caches whether demotion is allowed for this node and scan. It then loops over the input list yielding per folio, detaching each entry, retaining entries that fail try lock, handling poison with large folio retention versus unmap and drop for small poisoned folios, asserting inactive membership, accounting scanned base pages, and classifying dirty, writeback, unqueued dirty and congested counts before the truncated writeback discussion.

Observed state includes a vector with per LRU lists and a nonresident age; a scan control with reclaim index, order, unmap and deactivate permissions, skipped deactivate flag, target memcg, proactive and no demotion flags, priority and scanned count; a node with isolate counts, reclaim wait queues, writeback throttle counters and reclaim start; and a reclaim statistic with dirty, unqueued dirty, congested and demoted counts.

Batch and zone state observed includes a folio batch with count and array plus reinit semantics, a zone with per cpu sets and write pending and active and inactive file and anon snapshots, and a memcg with per cpu event storage and swap maximum.

Requeue and isolation face use after free and double queue hazards: isolation only clears LRU membership after pinning the folio and handles a lost clear race by dropping the pin; requeue sets membership before last reference test to avoid a race with concurrent release that skips locking when membership is clear.

Reclaim progress hazards include premature out of memory when ineligible folios dominate, unbounded skip scanning, and indefinite writeback stall. Mitigations observed are excluding skipped folios from progress accounting, bounding high zone diversions, splicing skipped entries to the head rather than tail, throttling when too many are isolated, and bypassing throttle under hopeless or low writeback conditions.

Counter families observed include node isolate deltas keyed by anon versus file, lruvec scan, steal, demote and rotate variants keyed by file type and by reclaimer identity with kswapd as base, plus refill, deactivate, scan skip and throttled written events. Exact numeric values are not shown in these fragments.

Limit and reason constants observed include a maximum zone count sizing per zone taken and skipped arrays, a bound on skipped high zone diversions to avoid lockup, per throttle reason identities for writeback, congested, no progress and isolated with distinct timeouts derived from HZ, and migrate type thresholds distinguishing isolate types and per cpu cache types with high types normalized to movable.
